titolo: FTX – Where Did $8 Billion of Customer Money Go?
descrizione:
In November 2022, the crypto exchange FTX collapsed within days, leaving a hole of roughly $8 billion between what customers were owed and what the company held. This documentary follows the money: how customer deposits ended up at a sister trading firm, how a token valued by its own creators became collateral, and how a single leaked balance sheet triggered a run.

The video is based on court documents from the 2023 criminal trial of Sam Bankman-Fried, SEC and CFTC complaints, the Chapter 11 filings of FTX Trading and the reports of the bankruptcy estate, and coverage by major newspapers. Only facts from these public sources are used.

copertina.scena_rosso: A single red figure stands behind a hidden back door, quietly pulling stacks of cash out of a vault toward a second building
copertina.scena_blu: A crowd of blue figures lines up at the front, holding phones and deposit slips, waiting to withdraw while the vault shows empty
copertina.scena_oro: A giant gold FTX coin cracks down the middle and money spills out through the fracture

fatti: Within about ten days in November 2022, FTX went from a roughly $32 billion valuation (January 2022 funding round) to bankruptcy
FTX filed for Chapter 11 on November 11, 2022, together with Alameda Research and about 130 affiliated entities
John J. Ray III, who had overseen Enron's liquidation, became CEO and said he had never seen such a complete failure of corporate controls
Prosecutors later said customers were owed about $8 billion that the company did not have
Open question: customer money was supposed to sit untouched, so where did it go?
Sam Bankman-Fried founded Alameda Research, a crypto trading firm, in 2017
He launched the FTX exchange in 2019 and moved its headquarters to the Bahamas in 2021
He owned the majority of Alameda while FTX customers deposited money on the exchange
Caroline Ellison became co-CEO of Alameda in 2021 and later CEO
FTX was backed by well-known investors, and its brand appeared in sports sponsorships and Super Bowl advertising
The January 2022 funding round valued FTX at about $32 billion
SBF presented himself as an advocate of regulation and testified before Congress in December 2021
FTX US was positioned as the regulated arm for American customers
FTX promised customers that their assets were held safely and not lent out
The FTX terms of service stated that customer assets remained customers' property
Prosecutors said a feature in the FTX code allowed Alameda to carry a negative balance and withdraw funds without limit
Alameda was effectively exempt from the automatic liquidation that applied to other traders
Gary Wang, FTX co-founder, and Nishad Singh, head of engineering, pleaded guilty and testified at trial
Customer deposits were routed through accounts controlled by Alameda
Prosecutors said Alameda used customer funds for trading, venture investments, real estate, and political donations

capitoli.titolo: A Token Worth Its Own Word
fatti: FTT was FTX's own exchange token, created by the company
Alameda held a large amount of FTT on its balance sheet
Alameda's assets leaked in November 2022 showed about $14.6 billion in total assets, with a big share in FTT and other illiquid holdings
Much of the value of FTT was therefore only as good as the market's belief in FTX itself
Alameda borrowed against these assets, so a drop in FTT could trigger a chain of losses
On November 2, 2022, CoinDesk published a report on Alameda's balance sheet
On November 6, Binance CEO Changpeng Zhao announced Binance would sell its FTT holdings
Customers withdrew about $6 billion from FTX in 72 hours, according to later reporting
SBF tweeted that FTX was fine and assets were fine, then deleted the post
FTX halted withdrawals on November 8, 2022
On November 8, Binance signed a non-binding letter of intent to buy FTX
Binance withdrew from the deal on November 9 after reviewing the books
FTX sought emergency funding from investors without success
FTX filed for bankruptcy on November 11, 2022, and SBF resigned as CEO
Customers lost access to their funds, and the bankruptcy covered over a million creditors
SBF was arrested in the Bahamas in December 2022 and extradited to the US
Caroline Ellison, Gary Wang, and Nishad Singh pleaded guilty and cooperated
The jury trial began in October 2023 in Manhattan federal court
On November 2, 2023, the jury found SBF guilty on all seven counts, including wire fraud and conspiracy
On March 28, 2024, he was sentenced to 25 years in prison and ordered to forfeit $11 billion
The bankruptcy estate recovered assets and reported it could repay creditors in full based on the November 2022 dollar value of claims
Many customers received repayment plus interest, but crypto prices had risen since 2022, so they received less than their holdings would be worth today
Money from customer deposits had gone to Alameda's trading losses, venture investments, loans to executives, real estate in the Bahamas, and political donations
Answer to the loop: customer money was lent to Alameda, a sister firm, and spent or lost, against FTX's own promises
Lesson: customer assets must be kept separate and audited independently; a founder who controls both exchange and trading firm removes the checks. Subscribe for the next one.
